summary: Klevdal–Patrikis show that, for Shimura data in the superrigid regime and neat level, the canonical ℓ-adic representations ρ_{y,ℓ}: Gal(Q̄/F) → G^ad(Q_ℓ) attached to a number-field point y form a compatible system (unramified outside N(y)ℓ, with Q-rational and equal semisimple Frobenius classes), deduced from compatibility of the canonical G(Q_ℓ)-local systems on connected Shimura varieties; this covers non-abelian type. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and ten findings are recorded, with corrections for the proof issues E1–E4; E8 is an arXiv v1 error that the published version corrects. Not formalised.

items.name: Centralizer of a dense adjoint image

items.statement: For the finite-field local systems in this argument, tame ramification is preserved by companions, using the curvewise tameness criterion and equality of Swan data. This is a separate consequence of Kerz–Schmidt Proposition4.2 and Deligne Theorem9.8.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Adjoint arithmetic density forces geometric density
items.statement: If the arithmetic image is dense in connected adjoint semisimple G, the Zariski closure H of geometric monodromy is normal. The quotient G/H is densely generated by one Frobenius, hence commutative; its semisimple adjoint structure forces it trivial.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Companion pullback kills the specialization kernel
items.statement: Pull the tame λ-companion back through surjective specialization and topological π₁. Geometric density and G-superrigidity identify it with τ∘ρ; consequently the original geometric λ-representation factors through tame specialization as well.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Integral-section inertia vanishes
items.statement: For every permitted number-field section through a fibre over p, equivariant tame specialization makes its inertia image centralize the dense geometric image. Adjointness then forces inertia to act trivially on the specialized λ-representation.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Ramification detected by a tangent direction
items.statement: If the lisse sheaf in Proposition2.3 fails to extend across the removed p-fibre of its regular arithmetic model, Drinfeld Corollary5.2 supplies a closed point z and a one-dimensional subspace V⊂T_z such that every suitable arithmetic curve with that tangent direction detects ramification.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Arithmetic section with prescribed tangent direction
items.statement: In the regular arithmetic situation of the ramification test, the Hilbert-irreducibility construction of Drinfeld Lemma5.3/Theorem2.15 produces a number-field section through z with tangent image V after residue-field extension and with the required generic intersection.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Uniform extension of the adjoint family
items.statement: Under the §2 good-compactification, dense integral representation, G-superrigidity, continuous descents and common-field hypothesis, there is N' divisible by N such that every ρ_λ factors uniquely through π₁(X_O_F[1/N'ℓ]). Arithmetic descent is proved by the tangent-curve contradiction, not from geometric factorization alone.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Fibrewise compatibility up to an algebraic automorphism
items.statement: Under Proposition2.3, for λ,λ' over ℓ,ℓ' and v∤N'ℓℓ', some τ(λ,λ',v)∈Aut(G_Qbar_λ') makes ρ_λ,v and τ∘ρ_λ',v companions. The automorphism may depend on all three parameters and need not yet be inner.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Density-one recognition for connected G-monodromy
items.statement: For the connected reductive, Zariski-dense finite-field systems of Remark2.5, agreement of rational semisimple classes on a density-one set of closed points is equivalent to companionship. Extend BHKT Proposition6.4 from curves using finite-field Chebotarev; do not drop connected monodromy.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Compatible symmetry-breaking section
items.statement: For λ,λ' and v as in Proposition2.3, choose C_y/F finite and y∈X(O_C_y[1/N_y]), where N_y is divisible by N' but not v. At every v_y|v its specializations have the same Qbar semisimple class, represented by an element fixed by no automorphism with nontrivial image in Out(G).

items.statement: The global Artin map on ideles of a number field is normalized so local uniformizers map to geometric Frobenius in the abelianized absolute Galois group. Import class field theory and explicitly invert a supplier normalized arithmetically.

items.name: Canonical models with special-point reciprocity
items.statement: The general canonical model over E(G,X) carries the right G(A_f)-action and satisfies σ[x,a]_K=[x,r_x(α)a]_K for special x and rec(α)=σ, with extension-field norms understood. Existence in non-abelian type is the general canonical-model theorem, not a PEL construction.

items.name: Neat level with discrete rational centre
items.statement: Neatness of K₀ is the representation-independent torsion-freeness condition on eigenvalues of associated rational arithmetic elements. Together with Z_G(Q) discrete in Z_G(A_f), it removes the central stabilizers needed here. Neatness alone does not make every adelic quotient action effective.

items.statement: For open normal K⊂K₀ with K₀ neat and the discrete-centre hypothesis, the level cover is finite étale with the effective right K₀/K-action. The connected component over E_K₀,s gives a deck subgroup; it need not remain geometrically connected over that field.

items.statement: Choose X⁺ and representatives a of G(Q)_+\G(A_f)/K. Then Sh_K(C)=⊔_a Γ_a\X⁺, Γ_a=G(Q)_+∩aKa⁻¹; the effective topological fundamental group is its adjoint image. The discrete-centre/neat hypotheses identify Γ_a with that image here.

items.name: Q-simple factors as Weil restrictions
items.statement: Every Q-simple adjoint group is Res_F/Q H^s for a finite extension F/Q and an absolutely simple adjoint H^s/F. Over algebraically closed Ω it decomposes over embeddings F→Ω. In the Shimura application Deligne's datum theory further makes F totally real.

items.name: Arithmeticity of the effective component group
items.statement: The adjoint image Γ of Γ_a is an arithmetic subgroup of G^ad(Q). Its intersections with Q-simple factors contain a normal product subgroup Γ_I of finite index, and this reduction preserves the density arguments used in Proposition3.3.

items.name: Borel density for these arithmetic groups
items.statement: For the noncompact-type adjoint groups supplied by a Shimura datum, the effective arithmetic subgroup Γ is Zariski dense. The application permits compact real factors inside a Q-simple restriction of scalars, but excludes compact Q-simple factors.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: One source factor per absolutely simple target
items.statement: For a dense map Γ→G^ad(Ω), restrictions to the commuting Γ_j have commuting normal Zariski closures in each absolutely simple adjoint target factor. Exactly one source Γ_j has dense image there; the other images are trivial.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Margulis algebraic extension in the source regime
items.statement: With Q-simple arithmetic Γ_j, S={∞}, real rank at least two and absolutely simple adjoint target over algebraically closed characteristic-zero Ω, Margulis VIII.3.4(a) gives an algebraic surjection after some extension Ω'/Ω realizing the dense representation. Ω'/Ω is not generally finite.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Surjective adjoint endomorphism is an automorphism
items.statement: Assemble the factor maps into η:G^ad_Ω'→G^ad_Ω'. Density makes η surjective; equal dimension and the absence of a central isogeny kernel for an adjoint group make η an isomorphism. This char-zero structural argument is not valid for arbitrary inseparable endomorphisms.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Extension from the finite-index arithmetic product
items.statement: The algebraic η agrees with ρ on Γ_I. For g∈Γ, the ratio η(g)⁻¹ρ(g) centralizes the dense η(Γ_I), so adjointness makes it one. Thus η realizes ρ on all Γ, not just the product subgroup.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Descent of the comparison automorphism
items.statement: After representing the outer class over algebraically closed Ω, reduce τ over Ω' to an inner conjugator g. Every automorphism of Ω'/Ω fixes g by density and trivial centralizer; use the fixed-field property for algebraically closed Ω to descend g and τ to Ω.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Higher-rank component groups are G-adjoint-superrigid
items.statement: For any neat level and Shimura datum whose Q-simple adjoint factors each have real rank at least two, the topological fundamental group of a connected component is G^ad-superrigid in Definition2.2, over every algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Higher-rank cohomological rigidity input
items.statement: For the arithmetic lattice and characteristic-zero representations in the introductory Margulis discussion, H¹(Γ,V)=0 supplies cohomological rigidity and finite abelianization, with the relevant boundary quasi-unipotence/unipotence input. The precise source theorem and admissible V must be extracted before exporting an unrestricted vanishing statement.

items.name: Uniform integrality of special points
items.statement: For fixed neat level, Pila–Shankar–Tsimerman–Esnault–Groechenig Theorem4.1 supplies a smooth integral model over O_E[1/N], obtained as a relative SNC complement in a smooth projective scheme, such that all special points extend over Zbar[1/N]. This is a soft model, not an integral canonical-model extension property.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Smooth connected-component integral model
items.statement: Take the closure of S_K₀,s in the chosen model and enlarge N to obtain a smooth model over O_E_K₀,s[1/N], retaining the selected integral special point. The component field is not replaced by the whole reflex field.

items.statement: For s=[x,a], identify Γ with topological π₁ via the right action y↦γ⁻¹y. The canonical adelic representation restricted to Γ sends γ to a⁻¹γa; after adjoint projection and ℓ-projection the comparison diagram commutes.

items.name: Uniform integral extension of canonical adjoint systems
items.statement: The canonical arithmetic local systems have the same field E_K₀,s for all ℓ. The Betti comparison, Borel density and Proposition3.3 discharge the abstract hypotheses, giving after one enlargement of N continuous ρ_ℓ:π₁(S_model[1/ℓ])→G^ad(Q_ℓ).

items.name: Canonical fibre companions up to outer ambiguity
items.statement: For ℓ,ℓ' and v∤Nℓℓ', the canonical adjoint systems on the v-fibre become companions after an automorphism τ∈Aut(G^ad_Qbar_ℓ'). This corollary does not yet prove compatibility without τ.

items.name: Irreducible rational torus
items.statement: A positive-dimensional torus T/k is irreducible if it has no nonzero proper k-subtorus; equivalently X*(T)⊗Q is an irreducible rational Galois representation. Integral lattice isomorphism and rational representation isomorphism are distinct.

items.name: Generic-torus Weyl and star-action Galois group
items.statement: For the generic torus of adjoint H, the splitting Galois action on its character lattice is W(H,T)⋊A₀, where A₀ is the image of the star-action. Retain that finite group and its action, not only its order.

items.name: Full generic Galois group at a rational torus
items.statement: Hilbert irreducibility on rational Tori_H yields a rational maximal torus T₀ whose character-lattice Galois image is the full generic W⋊A₀. The connected cover/splitting field and irreducibility hypotheses belong to this application.

items.name: Finite local witnesses force full Weyl image
items.statement: Prasad–Rapinchuk's auxiliary-place construction gives S' disjoint from a prescribed S such that matching T₀ locally at S' forces the desired full Galois image on the character lattice, up to a specified identification.

items.name: Weyl factors and transitive star-action imply irreducibility
items.statement: For Q-simple H=Res_F/Q H^s, X*(T)_Q decomposes over embeddings of F into Qbar. Each absolute Weyl factor acts irreducibly on its own summand, and A₀ acts transitively on the summands. Thus the full W⋊A₀ representation is irreducible.

items.name: Local conjugacy orbits of maximal tori are open
items.statement: For the local-field groups in Lemma3.6, the orbit inn(K_v)(T_v) for an open subgroup K_v is open in the maximal-torus variety. For a product H and arbitrary open K_v, first choose a product of open subgroups contained in K_v; do not assume K_v itself is a product (E3).

items.name: Auxiliary split–anisotropic separation
items.statement: For each unordered pair of distinct Q-simple adjoint factors choose a distinct auxiliary prime p_i,j where both groups split, outside p and any prescribed finite forbidden set. Choose a split maximal torus in one and an anisotropic maximal torus in the other, plus arbitrary maximal tori in remaining factors. Apply item090 to realize these local conjugacy classes together with the real and p-adic prescriptions. Choose the exceptional H¹ prime p₀ outside these primes. This strengthens the paper’s nonisomorphism condition to nonisogeny.

items.name: Rational character recognition for finite-image Galois modules
items.statement: Semisimple rational representations of Γ_Q with finite image and isomorphic restrictions at almost all decomposition groups are isomorphic over Q, by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt together with coefficient descent. This is stronger than merely an isomorphism over Qbar.

items.statement: For the torus-valued cocycle used in Proposition3.7, each T_i and T′_i are Q-isomorphic by item148. Their integral character modules, rational irreducibility and pairwise nonisogeny are therefore preserved. The paper’s local comparison plus Chebotarev/Brauer–Nesbitt remains an alternative proof; it is not needed for this particular twist.

items.name: Separated special torus factors
items.statement: Choose the auxiliary split–anisotropic prescriptions so the constructed T'_i are pairwise nonisogenous, hence pairwise nonisomorphic as required by the printed Proposition3.7(3). The stronger property is explicitly retained for the later direct-sum proof.

items.name: Unramified special torus at the selected prime
items.statement: The constructed T'_Qp is unramified, since it is Q_p-conjugate to the chosen unramified local torus. This alone does not establish integral position relative to the originally fixed hyperspecial model.

items.name: Dominant special Hodge cocharacter
items.statement: After descent to Qbar and extension along the selected embedding, μ' is dominant for a Q_p-rational Borel containing T'_Qp. Its adjoint projection is nonzero on every Q-simple factor; no claim of positivity on every simple root is made.

items.name: Ordinary interpretation of the constructed special datum
items.statement: In the Siegel case the unramified-torus/dominant-Hodge conditions give ordinary CM reduction at a suitable place. More generally apply BST Proposition9.10 for μ-ordinariness. This is a supplementary comparison and not an input from BST Theorem9.7 to the main proof.

items.name: Full adjoint Mumford–Tate torus
items.statement: Let T=∏T_i be a product of irreducible pairwise nonisogenous Q-tori and M⊂T a subtorus surjecting onto every T_i. Then M=T: each rational character summand injects into X*(M)_Q and pairwise inequivalence makes their sum injective. Applied to M_x^ad, nontrivial Hodge projection supplies each surjection. Use the strengthened E2 hypothesis.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Centralizer and unique rational torus factor
items.statement: From M_x^ad=T_x^ad obtain Cent_G(M_x)=T_x. The q in Lemma3.2 therefore lies in T_x(Q), and T_x(Q)∩aK₀a⁻¹={1} under the source neatness/discrete-centre hypotheses. Hence r_x(α)=q a k₀ a⁻¹ has a unique rational torus factor for fixed α.

items.name: Descent of an integral special point to its field
items.statement: For a separated finite-type model over O_L[1/N] and number field L, its O_L[1/N]-points equal the intersection of its L-points and its Zbar[1/N]-points inside the Qbar-points. Descend through a finite Galois extension using the categorical quotient of its ring-of-integers spectrum.

items.statement: For w∤Nℓ in E(s_K₀), an idele supported at w and the unique rational torus factor q give ρ_K₀,s,ℓ(Frob_w)=a_ℓ⁻¹q⁻¹a_ℓ. After adjoint projection and conjugation by a_ℓ this lies in T_x^ad(Q), with the same q for every ℓ≠char(w).

items.statement: Under the hypotheses of item146 and a Q_p-rational Borel as in item147, v_p(χ(N μ(π_L)))=e^-1∑σ<χ,σμ>. For each adjoint semisimple factor on which μ is nonzero, one simple root gives a positive value. This is a written general-uniformizer repair of the inference on journal pp328–329, conditional on the explicitly imported foundations; it does not prove the paper’s intermediate unramified-field assertion.

items.name: Infinite-order Frobenius in every adjoint factor
items.statement: Under Lemma3.9’s special-point integrality, reciprocity and rational-Borel dominance assumptions, using pairwise nonisogeny in its Mumford–Tate argument, every adjoint Q-simple projection of ρ_{ℓ,s}(Frob_w) has infinite order for ℓ≠p. No unramifiedness of E(s)_w/Q_p is needed for this conclusion. The original stronger hypotheses may be retained; item092 is not an input to this repaired implication.

items.name: Rational cyclic algebraic closure and base change
items.statement: For t∈T(Q), form the algebraic subgroup generated by t as the Q-Zariski closure of its integer powers. Its base change to Qbar_ℓ is the closure of those same powers there. This descent/base-change assertion is needed because the automorphism fixing t may be defined only over Qbar_ℓ.

items.name: Cyclic density in separated irreducible tori
items.statement: If T=∏T_i consists of pairwise nonisogenous irreducible Q-tori and t∈T(Q) has infinite-order image in every factor, the identity component of its cyclic closure surjects onto each factor and the rational-character direct-sum argument forces the closure to equal T. Infinite order in each factor alone fails for T₁×T₁.

items.name: An automorphism fixing a maximal torus pointwise is inner
items.statement: For connected reductive G over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, an algebraic automorphism acting identically on a maximal torus acts trivially on its root datum and is conjugation by a torus element. Import the reductive-group isomorphism theorem, not only the classification of abstract Dynkin diagrams.

Set Ntilde=NN₀N₁N₂; it is independent of ℓ,ℓ' and the fibre.

items.statement: For every v∤Ntildeℓℓ', choose the symmetry-breaking special point in the selected component and a place w|v induced by the chosen p-adic embedding. Its integral section supplies common rational Frobenius classes, and Proposition2.8 removes the fibrewise outer automorphism.

items.name: Number-field Chebotarev density input
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, every conjugacy class occurs as Frobenius at unramified primes with its prescribed positive density. Use this to test finite-image character representations and the field of definition of a quotient point.
items.note: The cited stage owns this scope; planned does not mean implemented or proof-closed.

items.name: Rationality of the common conjugation-quotient point
items.statement: For the common Qbar point α_x of G^ad//G^ad, its realizations lie in Q_ℓ for every embedding Qbar→Qbar_ℓ at almost all ℓ. A finite field of definition and Chebotarev force every Galois conjugate to coincide, hence α_x∈(G^ad//G^ad)(Q). No rational group representative is asserted.

items.name: Uniform adjoint compatibility on the soft integral model
items.statement: For (G,X) with discrete Z_G(Q)⊂Z_G(A_f), neat K₀ and real rank≥2 for every Q-simple factor of G^ad, the canonical adjoint systems extend to the smooth component model away from Nℓ. There is Ntilde such that for every ℓ,ℓ' and every closed x away from Ntildeℓℓ', their semisimple Frobenius classes equal one point of (G^ad//G^ad)(Q). Proof remains gated by E2,E4 repairs.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Field of the component containing a rational point
items.statement: If F contains the reflex field and y∈Sh_K₀(F), the geometrically connected component containing y is Γ_F-invariant, so its canonical definition field E_K₀,s lies in F. The point extends to the soft model over O_F[1/N(y)] after a finite enlargement.

items.name: Compatible systems at arbitrary number-field points
items.statement: Under Theorem3.10, for each number-field point y the specialized ρ_ℓ,y are unramified away from N(y)ℓ after incorporating Ntilde into N(y), and for every v∤N(y)ℓℓ' their semisimple Frobenius classes agree in (G^ad//G^ad)(Q). The exceptional integer may depend on y.

items.statement: An abelian Q-rational locally algebraic/Hodge–Tate torus-valued compatible family r_ℓ of the source's fixed-modulus type arises from a unique Q-algebraic map r:S_L,m→T. Construct it by tensor functoriality or characters and Chebotarev descent. items.statement: For non-adjoint G, different arithmetic extensions of one geometric system may differ by characters π₁(X_F)→Z_G(Qbar_λ), with ramification varying in λ. The unique-extension and uniform-ramification arguments for adjoint G therefore cannot be reused unchanged.

items.statement: Beyond central descent ambiguity, Margulis comparison for general reductive G can introduce a Γ→Z_Gder character, and equality on geometric π₁ need not determine the arithmetic companion. Compatibility after projection to G/Gder and G^ad alone is not asserted to imply full G-compatibility.

items.name: Rank-one and motivic boundaries of the result
items.statement: Theorems1.1/3.10 apply only in the stated higher-rank regime. They produce adjoint ℓ-adic compatibility, not Simpson motivicity, crystalline compatibility at ℓ=p, an integral canonical model, or full G-valued compatibility. The separately cited 2025 follow-ups are downstream results, not prerequisites.

items.statement: For a semisimple affine group in Hopf coordinates, adjointness means its centre-defining ideal equals the augmentation ideal, so the represented centre is the identity subgroup. Reuse this pinned object rather than declaring a second adjoint predicate.

items.name: Universally central adjoint points are identity
items.statement: For an adjoint semisimple Hopf-coordinate group, every universally central point over any commutative value algebra equals one. A point centralizing a Zariski-dense subset still needs the separate density-to-universal-centrality bridge.

items.name: Field norm as a product of embeddings
items.statement: For a finite separable extension L/K and an algebraically closed extension E/K, algebraMap K E (Algebra.norm K z) equals the product of σ(z) over all K-algebra embeddings σ:L→E. No normality or unramifiedness assumption.

items.name: Uniqueness of the extended absolute value
items.statement: Let K be complete, nontrivially normed and nonarchimedean, and L/K algebraic. Every real-valued absolute value on L restricting to the given norm of K equals spectralNorm K L pointwise. This is absolute-value uniqueness; the normalized additive finite-extension adapter remains item142.

items.name: Compact subsets of a discrete space are finite
items.statement: In a topological space X with DiscreteTopology, IsCompact s if and only if the subset s is finite.

items.name: Equivariant complements for finite groups
items.statement: For a finite group H and a field k in which Nat.card H is nonzero, every k[H]-submodule of a k[H]-module has an H-equivariant complement. In particular this applies to rational finite-image Galois representations.

items.name: Normalized valuations in finite extensions
items.statement: For finite L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, the extension valuation is unique up to normalization; v_L|K=e(L/K)v_K with e>0, and e f=[L:K]. For K=Q_p, the extension of v_p(p)=1 to an algebraic closure therefore satisfies v_p(σπ_L)=1/e for every K-embedding σ and every uniformizer π_L. Import the finite-extension construction, valuation-topology comparison and normalization from their existing owner.

items.note: AUDIT-04 records the normalized valuation and spectral uniqueness as built but the finite-extension local-field package and e/f adapters as partial/absent. Do not turn this planned theorem into a library claim.

items.name: Continuity of character evaluation on local points
items.statement: For a finite extension E/F of nonarchimedean local fields and a separated affine finite-type F-group T, the map T(F)→T(E) is continuous. Every E-algebraic character T_E→G_m induces a continuous homomorphism T(F)→E×. Closed subgroup inclusions are topological closed embeddings; hence T(F)∩C is compact for a compact subgroup C of an ambient affine group.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329
items.note: Read the complete RG2.0 layer: topology, functoriality, products, closed immersions and Hausdorffness. Its finite-extension scalar map is an instance of the chart construction; exact packet adapter remains G9.

items.name: Torus norm on points over a finite separable extension
items.statement: For a torus T/F and finite separable L/F inside Fbar, define N^T_L/F:T(L)→T(F) by N(t)=∏σ σ(t) over F-embeddings L→Fbar. The action on the L-rational point is independent of the extension of σ to Fbar. Commutativity makes the product Galois-fixed and hence F-rational. This is the point evaluation of the existing Weil-restriction norm, not a second carrier for tori or restriction of scalars.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329
items.note: Import affine Weil restriction and its splitting product from ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a; its general pointwise norm adapter is missing. The scalar field norm is item138, not the full torus norm.

api.name: AdjointCompatibility.torusnormpoint.product
api.statement: After extension to Fbar, N^T_L/F(t)=∏σ σ(t).

api.name: AdjointCompatibility.torusnormpoint.map
api.statement: For an F-homomorphism f:T→U, f(N^T_L/F(t))=N^U_L/F(f(t)).

api.name: AdjointCompatibility.torusnormpoint.tower
api.statement: For finite separable M/L/F and t∈T(M), N^T_M/F(t)=N^T_L/F(N^(T_L)_M/L(t)).

items.name: Geometric characters have zero valuation on compact subgroups
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field, T/F a torus, C⊂T(F) a compact subgroup, and χ a geometric character defined over a finite splitting extension E/F. Then v_E(χ(c))=0 for every c∈C. Consequently any positive rescaling of v_E, including the extension of v_p, also vanishes on χ(C). No integral model of T or maximality of C is assumed.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329

items.name: Pairing formula for a ramified torus norm
items.statement: Let L/Q_p be finite, π_L a uniformizer, T/Q_p a torus and μ∈X_*(T_L). For any χ∈X*(T_Qpbar), normalized by v_p(p)=1, v_p(χ(N^T_L/Qp(μ(π_L))))=e(L/Q_p)^-1∑σ:L→Qpbar <χ,σμ>. The sum counts embeddings with multiplicity, even when several induce the same cocharacter. There is no claim that the norm point equals (∑σ σμ)(p).
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329

items.name: A Galois orbit of dominant cocharacters has a positive root pairing
items.statement: Let H/F be a connected adjoint semisimple group over a characteristic-zero field, T⊂B⊂H an F-rational maximal torus and Borel, and μ a geometric cocharacter defined over finite L/F. If μ is B-dominant and its projection to an F-defined semisimple factor H_i is nonzero, then some B_i-simple root α has ∑σ:L→Fbar <α,σμ_i>>0. All terms of this particular sum are nonnegative. Strict positivity for every simple root is unnecessary.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329

items.name: A torus-valued conjugation cocycle gives a rational torus isomorphism
items.statement: Let F have characteristic zero, G/F be an affine algebraic group, T⊂G an F-torus and g∈G(Fbar). If cσ=gσ(g)^-1∈T(Fbar) for every σ∈Γ_F, then T′=g^-1Tg and φ:T→T′, t↦g^-1tg, descend to F, and φ is an F-isomorphism. If G has F-defined normal factors, φ respects their projected tori. Thus integral as well as rational character Galois modules are isomorphic.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329
items.note: This is a worker-derived strengthening of the descent calculation printed on p326, not a separate author-stated theorem. Apply after mapping g and its Tsc-valued cocycle from Gsc to G.

items.name: Split and anisotropic local tori separate rational isogeny classes
items.statement: Let T_i,T_j be positive-dimensional Q-tori with irreducible rational character modules. If at some finite place v one is split and the other anisotropic, their rational Γ_Q-character modules are nonisomorphic and Hom_ΓQ(X*(T_i)_Q,X*(T_j)_Q)=0. It follows that the global tori are not isogenous.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329

items.name: Order is reflected by extension of fields
items.statement: For an affine group scheme H/F and an extension K/F, H(F)→H(K) is injective. For h∈H(F) and integer n>0, h^n=1 if and only if its image has nth power 1. Thus finite or infinite order is preserved by field extension, inversion and conjugation.
items.locator: Continuation: explicit repair of Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, journal pp325–329
